full_judgment: 14. It appears that the District Delegate failed to appreciate the principle relating of grant of Probate. In the instant was PW1 recipient of the 'Will' has deposed stating that her mother executed the 'Will' and she herself proved the 'Will' in question. She further stated that her two sisters namely Sreemoti Chandana and Sreemoti Koly Rani were witnesses in the sister Chandana deposed as PW.2 and while deposing she stated that her mother wrote the 'Will' herself and executed the same. Hence the PWs proved execution of the 'Will'. It appears that Koly has put her signature in the declaration of substantive application being filed for Probate of the `Will'. Learned District Delegate committed error in not relying the evidence of those witnesses who are reliable and trustworthy. The District Delegate found that inspite of service of summons the sons of the propounder of 'Will' did not turn up to controvert the contention of the which also signifies that they are also not opposing the Will'. The test before the Court is, while determining the question as to whether the instrument produced before the Court is the last 'Will' of the testator, the Court is thereby deciding a solemn question and it must be fully satisfied that it had been validly executed by the testator. The test is satisfaction of judicial conscience. No hard and fast or inflexible rules can be laid down for appreciation of such evidence. From the proof of the signature of the deceased it will be presumed that the testator knew the provisions of the instrument he has signed and that presumption is liable to be rebutted by proof of suspicious circumstances. What is a suspicious circumstance is a question of fact depending on the peculiar circumstances of each case. Suspicious can never be allowed to prevail over evidence and circumstances.
